title: Firehall Donair Platter
shortDescription: Spiced beef cones roasted and shaved with sweet sauce for ten
subtitle: Spiced beef cones roasted and shaved with sweet sauce for ten
description: Seasoned ground beef is pressed around vertical skewers, roasted until crisp-edged, then shaved thin for donair platters. Serve with warm pita, diced tomatoes, onions, and sweet garlicky donair sauce.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Firehall Donair Platter in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch beef. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Season the meat
steps.instruction: Mix beef, lamb if using, garlic powder, onion powder, oregano, paprika, salt, and pepper until sticky and uniform. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Form the cones
steps.instruction: Press seasoned meat around metal skewers or dowels set in loaf pans, packing tight into cone shapes about 6 inches tall. Plan about 20 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Roast until browned
steps.instruction: Roast at 350°F, rotating pans, until exterior is deeply browned and internal temp hits 165°F, about 50–60 minutes. Target oven/smoker temperature: 350°F.

steps.title: Make donair sauce
steps.instruction: Whisk condensed milk, vinegar, and garlic until smooth and tangy. Thin with a tablespoon of water if too thick. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 145°F for medium beef, 160°F for ground. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Firehall Donair Platter onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Shave and serve
steps.instruction: Rest cones 10 minutes, shave meat thin with a sharp knife, and pile on platters with warmed pita, tomatoes, onions, and sauce at the line.

proTips: A little baking soda in the mix helps bind—just a quarter teaspoon for the batch.
Offer lettuce for crew who want crunch without turning it into a generic wrap bar.
Save rendered fat from the pan to crisp pita edges on the griddle.
tonightSpread: Shaved donair meat with pita, tomatoes, onions, and sweet sauce.
Garlic fingers or fries on the side for the full Halifax-style spread.
leftovers: Reheat shaved meat in a skillet with sauce for quick donair bowls over rice—not the same as a burrito bowl, just honest leftovers.
Stuff into sub rolls for donair cheesesteaks on the next shift.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Donair is a Canadian hall legend—messy, satisfying, and impossible to eat quietly. Shaved meat platters let crews build wraps fast or plate it open-face when tones drop mid-meal.
mealPrepNotes: Form meat cones the night before on skewers set in loaf pans for stability. Donair sauce keeps 5 days refrigerated. Hold shaved meat at 165°F with a light broth mist.
